record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery after unlearning with a fixed-budget relearning fine-tune and matched behavioral evaluation; it does not reproduce the cited attacks or use their measures exactly.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own relearning attack trains on 50 forget documents. Mentions of benign-data recovery and quantization recovery in the introduction are citations to other work, not this paper’s results. It does not test activation-direction ablation, quantization recovery, or prompting-only recovery.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own fixed-budget relearning attack on WMDP-unlearned checkpoints of 12 methods across four models. It fine-tunes LoRA adapters on 50 forget documents and reports forget-accuracy recovery (Table 39, Table 40). This is a different method from the originals, aimed at whether forgetting is durable. The main contribution is a structural diagnostic (TRIAGE), but the recovery results bear directly on versions A and B.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The paper's main conclusion is that similar behavioral forgetting can hide very different parameter-space changes (no-op, partially localized, collateral dominant, globally destructive), and that these vary by model and benchmark. On relearning, the authors find that structurally active, non-collapsed checkpoints are readily reversible. They read low recovery in collapsed checkpoints as collapse, not robustness, but note Zephyr GA as a counterexample. They state that CoFi shifts are not a certificate of removal.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces TRIAGE and evaluates several unlearning recipes rather than reproducing one of the cited studies. The recovery attack fine-tunes LoRA adapters on 50 forget documents for 5 epochs, with a global cap of 500 optimizer steps; the attack uses the same parameter subspace as unlearning.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies across methods and models; globally destructive models often recover little, while Zephyr GA is an exception where fine-tuning also repairs general accuracy. Only one relearning budget is tested.

fits_no_version.finding: Forget-corpus CoFi shift correlates with relearning recovery across 11 Llama-3.1-8B checkpoints (Spearman ρ=0.65, p=0.030; Pearson r=0.76 among non-destructive ones).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The parameter-sensitivity footprint of unlearning on the forget corpus predicts how much knowledge a relearning attack recovers.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen3-32B, nearly all methods left WMDP forget accuracy at or above base (Tables 37–38), while some had nonzero CoFi shifts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard unlearning recipes may fail to suppress targeted knowledge at all on larger models under fixed hyperparameters.

record.problems: The relearning attack uses a single budget with no strength sweep, and recovery results have no uncertainty intervals reported. It fine-tunes on forget documents rather than unrelated or loosely related data. SPUL was not attacked. Some low-recovery results are confounded by model collapse; Zephyr GA recovery also raises general accuracy. Behavioral evaluation for other models uses a randomly selected subset of 40 questions per set.
record.rows_left_out: Kept 8 selected Llama-3.1-8B behavioral rows from Table 38 to represent target forgetting and general utility, and all 44 attacked-checkpoint recovery rows from Table 39. Other individual behavioral accuracies in Tables 36–38, the full CoFi/CHess/perplexity results in Tables 1 and 10–35, and the Table 40 per-partition post-attack accuracies were not extracted because the 60-row limit prioritizes the claim’s recovery outcome and representative evidence for version A.

untested.parts: Only one simple attack (relearning on forget documents) at one budget. No prompting, quantization or probing attacks.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data is not tested; only a subset of forget documents is used. No budget sweep. SPUL not attacked.
No activation-direction ablation. CoFi/CHess are structural diagnostics, not tests of blocked access versus deletion.
No quantization attack (quantization recovery is only cited).
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
No method is presented or tested as robust to these attacks.

missing.what: Post-unlearning → post-relearning per-partition accuracies showing forget accuracy returns to base (e.g. RMU Bio 0.329→0.694, Adaptive-RMU 0.269→0.687) while general stays flat
Pre-attack WMDP/MMLU accuracies for Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen3-32B and Zephyr. These are needed to judge whether each checkpoint forgot anything; Qwen methods mostly did not.

record.verdict_notes: Rows B* linked to A carry B-oriented states: 'observed' recovery means A's 'attacks don't recover' clause fails. The record's A 'challenges' label wrongly included B38 (Zephyr Adaptive-RMU, negligible forgetting). The record's Qwen 'limits_scope' for A/B was based on checkpoints that never forgot anything, so those rows are cannot_determine. The 40-question behavioral subsets for non-Llama-8B models make small recoveries (~0.03–0.06) noisy. The relearning set is a subset of forget documents, which is within version B's wording.

versions.untested_parts: Tests behavioral forgetting and general accuracy for selected WMDP results, plus one fixed-budget relearning attack. Does not establish near-chance forgetting with preserved ability across all methods or test other simple attacks.
The relearning set is 50 forget documents, not unrelated or loosely related examples; only one attack budget is tested, with no strength sweep.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing blocked access rather than deletion.
No quantization attack on unlearned weights.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context-only recovery attack.
The paper compares unlearning methods but does not test a newer method’s resistance to the attacks named in the claim.
